findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark colour-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-preference screenshot remains a light surface and the computed html color-scheme is normal; no dark retint is visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and provide preference-driven surface/text tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Non-essential animation continues when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe reports five running 1,000ms blinker animations while matchMedia(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) is true.
findings.suggestedFix: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, remove blinking/looping animation and disable non-essential auto-motion.

findings.summary: Route and prominent state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: CSS recon found no view-transition rules on a multi-route site; navigation is implemented as conventional document swaps.
findings.suggestedFix: Add same-document or cross-document View Transitions to preserve spatial continuity, with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: A large consent interstitial obscures the primary content on every sampled entry page.
findings.evidence: Mobile screenshots show a fixed role=dialog covering most of the viewport before users can read or act on homepage, listing, article, or subscription content.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, content-first consent surface with equal, immediately actionable choices and avoid re-covering each fresh page context.

findings.summary: The mobile page uses a fixed 940px layout viewport and scales the desktop layout down.
findings.evidence: At a requested 360x800 viewport, layout metrics report clientWidth/innerWidth 940 and visual scale 0.383; screenshots show tiny navigation and body text rather than true reflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Set viewport content to width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and replace fixed desktop sizing with fluid/intrinsic responsive layouts.

findings.summary: Mobile loading is slow despite acceptable visual stability.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports LCP 6.0s, Speed Index 8.2s, TTI 12.1s and performance 60; the trace corroborates 120ms TBT and one 170ms long task.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP asset, shorten critical chains, defer below-fold scripts/media, and measure field LCP/INP after release.

findings.summary: Critical delivery includes multiple blocking styles/scripts and substantial unused code.
findings.evidence: HAR flags six VeryHigh-priority parser styles plus synchronous scripts; Lighthouse estimates 300 KiB unused JS and 47 KiB unused CSS, and HAR lists missing cache headers.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical CSS, defer non-critical styles/scripts, split per-template bundles, and add durable caching to versioned assets.

findings.summary: Some interactive links and images lack accessible names or alternatives.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse finds four focusable links without discernible names and four dashboard images without alt attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every focusable link a meaningful accessible name; add informative alt text or alt=""/presentation for decorative images.

findings.summary: Consent controls and editorial labels fail minimum colour contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports consent links at 3.47:1, reject button at 3.02:1, green headline text at 2.65:1 and sponsored-content text at 2.35:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken foreground/accent colours or adjust backgrounds to meet WCAG AA in normal, dark and high-contrast conditions.

findings.summary: Key templates lack a clear main landmark and/or page-level heading.
findings.evidence: DOM probes found no main landmark on sampled pages and no H1 on homepage, news listing, or subscription landing page; the article alone exposes an H1.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap primary content in main and add one descriptive H1 per template while retaining the existing visible keyboard outlines.

findings.summary: The main response lacks a Content-Security-Policy and Referrer-Policy.
findings.evidence: Header probe confirms HTTPS, HSTS, nosniff and SAMEORIGIN, but reports CSP missing and Referrer-Policy missing.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP (including frame-ancestors) and an explicit strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter Referrer-Policy.

findings.summary: The initial page spends most transferred bytes on media and reaches many third-party origins before consent.
findings.evidence: HAR transfers 5.19 MB across 60 requests, including 2.91 MB media and 1.01 MB images; tracker recon sees 10 third-party origins in the pre-consent state.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not fetch video until it is visible or user-initiated, use posters first, enforce media/third-party budgets, and defer non-essential origins until consent.

findings.summary: The public site has no sitemap at the conventional sitemap.xml endpoint and suppresses snippets.
findings.evidence: robots.txt is reachable and allows general indexing, but /sitemap.xml returns HTTP 404; homepage metadata includes googlebot nosnippet.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a current XML sitemap and reference it from robots.txt; reconsider nosnippet where rich result/search preview reach matters.

findings.summary: The subscription landing surface promotes benefits and a purchase CTA without showing price or commitment in the visible offer.
findings.evidence: The subscription mobile screenshot and text probe show feature bullets and “Prøv Ekstra Bladet+”/purchase actions but no price, billing period or renewal terms on the landing surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Place price, billing cadence, trial/renewal terms and cancellation path adjacent to the primary subscription CTA before checkout.

Make the consent experience compact, accessible and content-first
Fix accessible names, alt text, landmarks and headings
Add dark and reduced-motion preference support
Deploy CSP and explicit referrer policy
Publish sitemap/indexing signals and expose complete subscription terms
Add View Transitions with reduced-motion fallback
